clue.text: Phone model checked by its manufacturer before daughter used

indicators.note: a maker checking its product holds it under inspection, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: the company that makes the iPhone
the one-letter prefix in the name of Apple's handset, the i of iPhone
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A phone gets inspected at the factory before it is handed on to a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone model' suggests a whole handset, but only the little i that prefixes the iPhone's name is needed, held inside its maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something applied has been put to use, so the past participle matches 'used'.

clue.text: Player lowering the tone maybe, scratching head and back

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the opening letter

blocks.note: a musician who plays the low notes

explanation.surface: A rowdy musician spoils the atmosphere, scratching their head and their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowering the tone' suggests bad behaviour, but a bassist literally supplies the low tones.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support them, which is what assist means as a verb.

clue.text: In exercise, fall behind for all to see, getting pain in the neck

indicators.note: the following pieces go in the word for exercise

blocks.note: physical education
to fall behind is to lag
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: During a workout, someone lagging behind in public view ends up with a stiff neck.
explanation.walkthrough: A U certificate is the British film rating suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a nuisance, used informally as a noun just as a pain in the neck is.

clue.text: Essential to redesign Private Eye's cover – Dharma's on it!

indicators.note: the cover of a magazine is its outside front, so the first letter
a redesign arranges the parts in a new form

blocks.note: the setter Dharma refers to themselves: I'm
the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be working on a vital makeover of Private Eye, the British satirical magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on it' puts the setter's I'M on top of the rearranged letters. Private Eye is a British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperative as an adjective means vitally necessary, a synonym of essential.

clue.text: Club not very but increasingly teetotal

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for very is absent from the word

blocks.note: a driver is a golf club
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A social club is no longer heavy drinking, becoming more and more alcohol-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry describes someone who abstains from alcohol, so the comparative means more teetotal.

clue.text: Save hard with The Telegraph Group

blocks.note: H is the pencil grade for hard
how the newspaper's own staff would refer to themselves
a band is a group

explanation.surface: An advert urging readers to save money with the newspaper's corporate group.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes for The Telegraph, so from the paper's own point of view it is 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is an old verb meaning to manage them thriftily, that is to save them.

clue.text: Seething over procedure held up thanks to delicate issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up turns it to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: seething with anger is hot under the collar
an operation, a surgical procedure
ta is British slang for thanks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fuming about a delayed process that has created a sensitive matter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places HOT above the rest. OP reverses to PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial matter that is awkward to handle.

clue.text: Satisfied, waves France away for Spain

indicators.note: one letter goes away and another takes its place

blocks.note: surf is breaking waves
F is the international code for France
E is the international code for Spain

explanation.surface: A happy holidaymaker waves goodbye to France and heads for Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied that something is true means being sure of it, without doubt.

clue.text: Fellow rogue, after a sin, turned up expressing first sign of remorse

indicators.note: expressing literally means pressing out, so a letter is squeezed from the word
in a down clue, turning up flips a word so it reads upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a cad is a dishonourable man
a crime is a wrongdoing
the first letter of remorse

explanation.surface: A rogue turns up full of remorse after committing a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIME with its R pressed out is CIME, which reads upward as EMIC beneath A and CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a senior member of a college, an academic of standing.

clue.text: Careful individual speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: discrete means separate, individual

explanation.surface: A cautious person talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A discreet person is circumspect and guarded in what they say, so careful.

clue.text: Bog trade, plumber's heart's in it

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
something being in it means the second piece is placed inside the first

blocks.note: to trade is to swap
the middle letter of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A plumber's trade is all about the bog, a British slang word for toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet, which suits a plumber in the surface, but here it means marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is soft waterlogged ground, the same sort of wetland as a swamp.

clue.text: Breaks leg, ignoring pain to begin with and travels abroad

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped
points to the opening letter of the word for pain as the one dropped
abroad suggests being scattered far from home, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
the first letter of pain, which is removed
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a leg, gets past the pain and goes travelling overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is British slang for legs, as in 'unsteady on his pins'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervals are pauses between the parts of a performance, so breaks in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Perhaps two to four old-fashioned causes finally ditched

indicators.note: the final letter is thrown away, so the word is cut short at the end

blocks.note: square means conventional and uncool
the roots of a problem are its causes

explanation.surface: Some outdated causes have at last been abandoned, a reading the opening numbers seem to interrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOTS loses its last letter. 'Two to four' looks like a time or a score, but two is the square root of four.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself makes four, so two stands in the square-root relation to four, an example of the term.

clue.text: Periodically in Le Havre, or close

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Something happens now and then in the French port of Le Havre, or somewhere close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Near and close are synonyms when describing something at a short distance.

clue.text: Regret road rages in reverse!

indicators.note: something raging is out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that road rage leads to regret, phrased as backwards advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde describes motion that goes backwards, so it means in reverse.

clue.text: Addition to half of refrain by legendary guitarist with two notes out of sequence?

blocks.note: to refrain is to stop
Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin
the sol-fa notes me and ti, put in the opposite order to the scale

explanation.surface: A musical note on a chorus played by a famous guitarist with two notes jumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: In the sol-fa scale me comes before ti, so TI then ME is out of sequence. Stoppage time is added on at the end of each half of a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra minutes added for injuries and delays at the end of a football half are called stoppage time.

clue.text: Material for each marquee in parts

indicators.note: something that parts splits open to let something else in

blocks.note: per means for each
a marquee is a large tent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fabric for each big tent is divided into sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth for the marquee, but it is the adjective meaning relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Material evidence is evidence relevant to the case, so material is a synonym of pertinent.

clue.text: Permissible to support character backing Kemi, Jenrick for one suggested

indicators.note: the character at the back of a name is its final letter

blocks.note: the last character of the name
Robert Jenrick is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A political story about who is allowed to back Kemi Badenoch, with Robert Jenrick as an example of a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue LICIT supports, sitting under, IMP. Kemi Badenoch and Robert Jenrick are senior British Conservative politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied rather than stated, which is what suggested means.

clue.text: Banked 100, scored batting first

blocks.note: a batsman who is batting is in
C is the Roman numeral for 100
to score a surface is to mark it with lines

explanation.surface: A cricketer banks a century, having scored it while batting first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves IN to the front. In cricket a batsman at the crease is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: A banked road or track is inclined, sloping at an angle.

clue.text: One hitting the drink maybe in deep trouble?

definitions.text: One hitting the drink maybe in deep trouble?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who drinks heavily, hitting the bottle
setter's reading: a sailor who has fallen into the sea and is in danger in the deep

explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' and 'the deep' are both slang for the sea, so the heavy drinker in trouble is really someone who has fallen off a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry raised when a person falls off a vessel into the water, used here for that person.

clue.text: Parents casually purchasing a hat

indicators.note: purchasing means getting hold of something, so the outer pieces hold it

blocks.note: Pa 'n' Ma, an informal way of saying father and mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad buy a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat originally made in Ecuador.

clue.text: I'm surprised, very much so

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: truly, emphatically

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one person agreeing in surprise; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an interjection the word expresses surprise, and as an adverb it intensifies, meaning truly or very.

clue.text: Woman that amused me texted 'what gets Annie going'

indicators.note: whatever starts the name off is its opening letter

blocks.note: laugh out loud, the texting abbreviation
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A woman sends a message about what motivates her friend Annie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lola is a woman's first name, standing for any woman in crossword convention.

clue.text: Current Republican leaving venture for minimal reward from Labour?

indicators.note: something leaving departs from the word, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: current as in in present use, like a living language
R is the abbreviation for Republican
to venture money is to wager it

explanation.surface: A US politician quits a business venture, the sort of thing the British Labour Party might comment on.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour suggests the British political party, but here it means work. R leaves WAGER to give WAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A living wage is the lowest pay enough to live on, the minimal reward for work.

clue.text: Passive tense, popular with former queen at first

blocks.note: in means fashionable
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on passive voice and tense, with a mention of a past queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' moves the popular piece and the queen ahead of tense. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual former queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means inactive and lacking the power to act, which is being passive.

clue.text: Centre touched down, wingers nowhere to be seen

indicators.note: the wingers are the outer letters, and they vanish

blocks.note: in rugby, touching down scores a try

explanation.surface: A rugby centre touches down for a try with no wingers around.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre and wingers are rugby positions, which hides that 'Centre' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its central part, a synonym for centre.

clue.text: Asian beat charged with notes agitato

indicators.note: something charged with a load is filled with it, so the second piece goes inside
a musical direction meaning agitated, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: to beat with a stick is to cane
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Asian musician's rhythm is loaded with agitated musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Agitato is an Italian performance direction, which hides it among the musical words of the surface; the shuffled letters sit before the final letter of the beating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese means from Canton in southern China, so it is Asian in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Cricket items openers discounted remotely

indicators.note: the opening letters are discounted, that is left out

blocks.note: one item of cricket equipment
the other item of cricket equipment

explanation.surface: Cricket gear sold cheaply, opening batsmen's kit going at a discount, though only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT and BALL each lose their first letter. 'Openers' suggests opening batsmen but means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'if it's remotely possible', remotely means in the least, the same as 'at all'.

clue.text: Most smart papers joined with another engaged in research

indicators.note: being engaged in something means being occupied inside it

blocks.note: identity papers
another paper: the i, a British newspaper
research involves testing

explanation.surface: Academic papers are combined with another as part of a research project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another paper: the i is a British national newspaper, so it follows identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart can mean neat and well groomed, so the most smart is the tidiest.

clue.text: Stormzy's back following music style introduced by The Cure

indicators.note: the back of a name is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
rap is a genre of music
the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: The British rapper Stormzy's backing band and The Cure, the rock group, appear in one musical line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure looks like the name of the band, but 'The' joins the wordplay and Cure alone is the definition. Stormzy is a British rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment meant to heal, so it is a cure in the broad sense.
